name: Baobabs and the ginkgo — ancient landmark trees
status: 4 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: All 8 baobab species (Africa, Madagascar, Australia) and the ginkgo. Both are 'landmark' trees: individually rare, huge or ancient, worth a place name; the events/lore system may name them. Baobabs are bat-pollinated night-bloomers and shed leaves in the dry season; hollow old ones shelter camps and bees. Ginkgo turns gold and drops every leaf in a week.

canopy.name: African baobab

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling has broad cotyledons and simple, undivided first leaves; hand-shaped leaves with 3, then 5-7 leaflets come later. Young baobabs look nothing like adults: a slender, straight, tapering grey-green whip over a swollen tuberous taproot, with thin branches; the huge bottle trunk and wide crown form only after decades. Seeds are hard and germinate slowly unless scarified.
growth.source: Ethiopian Forestry Dev. baobab study (simple juvenile leaves, 5-7-foliate adult leaves, trees over 1000 yr); Anjarwalla et al. 2021 bioRxiv (seed-grown trees first flower at 8-23 yr; acid-treated seed sprouts in ~5 d); Patrut et al. 2018 Nature Plants (radiocarbon ages to ~2500 yr); height curve estimated

canopy.source: African savanna, Sahel to Limpopo. The upside-down tree; thousands of years old; hollow trunks shelter people and bees. All 8 Kew-accepted species. Deciduous in the dry season, bat-pollinated white flowers at night, fruit by mammals.

traits.leaf_shape: compound or lobed leaves in a flat spreading crown

bark.notes: smooth, shiny, folded and wrinkled grey to pink-grey, like elephant skin; coppery-pink patches where the surface sloughs; fibrous inside

leaf.notes: hand-shaped compound leaves of 5-7 leaflets radiating from one point; medium green; present only in the wet season

flower.form: big pendulous white flowers 15-20 cm with crumpled petals and a ball of stamens, opening at night, browning by morning

fruit.form: large egg-shaped pods 15-25 cm, velvety yellow-grey-brown, hanging on long stalks; chalky white pulp

appearance.seasonal: deciduous, bare for most of the dry season (8-9 months); leaves flush at the rains
appearance.silhouette: the upside-down tree: a vast grey bottle trunk with a spreading tangle of thick, stubby, root-like branches; leafless most of the year
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Adansonia digitata; Kew POWO; PlantZAfrica

fruiting.source: Venter & Witkowski 2019 For Ecol Manage (southern Africa: flowering 1-5 months peaking Nov, 290-710 flowers per tree, fruit set ~20%); EFD Ethiopia study (57-157 fruits/tree in Benin, 77 in South Africa); Baum 1995 (pendent white flowers open at dusk for one night, fruit-bat pollination)

canopy.name: Grandidier's baobab

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings have simple first leaves before digitate leaves with many leaflets. Young trees are straight, slender, fast whips (about 2 m in 2 years) with smooth grey-green bark and thin horizontal branches. The massive, smooth, reddish-grey cylindrical trunk with a flat-topped crown of branches develops only after decades.
growth.source: Useful Tropical Plants (2 m tall within 2 yr from seed; 12-15 m and 60 cm bole at 12 yr in cultivation); worldplants.ca (germination 2-6 weeks); simple juvenile leaves as in other baobabs; first flowering and age estimated from A. digitata and Patrut radiocarbon work on Malagasy baobabs

canopy.source: SW Madagascar dry forest; the Avenue. Tall smooth cylinders with a flat crown. All 8 Kew-accepted species. Deciduous in the dry season, bat-pollinated white flowers at night, fruit by mammals.

bark.notes: smooth, pale grey to reddish-grey, faintly ringed horizontally on huge cylinder; flushes pink-red in low sun

leaf.notes: palmately compound, 9-11 narrow blue-green leaflets, hairy; brief

flower.form: white flowers with a prominent stamen brush, opening at dusk

fruit.form: large oval fruit 20-30 cm, russet velvet, hanging in the crown

appearance.seasonal: deciduous, leafless most of the year (dry season); leaves briefly in the wet season
appearance.silhouette: a smooth untapering grey cylinder 25-30 m tall crowned by a small flat table of horizontal branches at the very top; the Avenue of the Baobabs
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Adansonia grandidieri; Kew POWO; Baum 1995 Ann Missouri Bot Gard

fruiting.source: Wikipedia/Baum 1995 (dry-season flowering May-Aug before the leaves; erect white flowers open at dusk with a brush of 600-700 filaments; pollinated by fork-marked lemurs and hawkmoths; rounded fruits with a 2-4.5 mm shell and dense reddish-brown hairs, ripe Nov-Dec); worldplants.ca (fuzzy green unripe)

canopy.name: Boab

growth.juvenile_note: The seedling forms a swollen, carrot-like (edible) tuberous root and simple, entire first leaves; compound leaves with 5-7 leaflets come later. Young boabs are thin, straight whips, often several-stemmed after fire or browsing; the bottle-shaped trunk swells slowly over decades and the tree drops its leaves each dry season.
growth.source: ANPSA (small spreading tree to ~12 m; the Kings Park boab estimated ~750 yr old); seed dormancy study in Seed Sci Res (hard seed); tuberous seedlings and simple juvenile leaves as in other baobabs; growth rate and first flowering estimated from A. digitata

canopy.source: Kimberley, NW Australia. Swollen bottle trunk; prison tree. All 8 Kew-accepted species. Deciduous in the dry season, bat-pollinated white flowers at night, fruit by mammals.

flower.form: large white flowers with crumpled petals and a stamen ball, opening at night

fruit.form: round to oval woody fruit 10-20 cm, tan-brown velvet, on long stalks

appearance.seasonal: deciduous in the dry season (May to October), bare grey silhouette; leaves in the wet

appearance.refs: Wikipedia Adansonia gregorii; Kew POWO; Australian Plant Society

fruiting.source: ANPSA (large white perfumed flowers mainly in the wet season; oval woody fruit to 180 mm with many seeds in edible pulp); Aust J Bot 64:678, 2016 ('Promiscuous pollination of Australia's baobab': hawkmoths plus diurnal visitors); ripening, fruit set and crop estimated from A. digitata

canopy.name: Ginkgo

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal: the cotyledons stay inside the big seed; the shoot comes up with a few fan-shaped leaves that are often deeply notched into two or more lobes. Young trees are gawky, sparsely branched spires with a strong leader and a few long, widely spaced branches; the crown fills out and broadens only after several decades.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Ginkgo biloba: 20-35 m, some >40 m; specimens >1600 yr, largest estimated >3500 yr; conical crown when young, broader and irregular with age); Del Tredici (ginkgo ecology). Growth-age curve and first-seed age from horticultural records (females bear at ~20-30 yr).

canopy.source: Wild in the Tianmu and Dalou mountains of E China; the last of its line, unchanged since the dinosaurs. Fan leaves turn pure gold in one week each autumn, then drop all at once. Dioecious; wind-pollinated; fetid seeds carried by mammals. Kew POWO.

traits.native_range: Wild in the Tianmu and Dalou mountains of E China
traits.leaf_shape: simple or compound broad leaves, most deciduous in cold bands
traits.trunk: single trunk dividing into a rounded crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.notes: grey to grey-brown, corky, deeply furrowed into irregular ridges on old trunks; pale grey smooth when young

leaf.notes: flat fan leaves with a notch, fine forking parallel veins, clustered on short spur shoots; bright fresh green

flower.form: small yellowish catkin-like pollen cones on males; tiny paired ovules on females

fruit.form: plum-like round seeds 2-3 cm, yellow-orange, fleshy and foul-smelling when they fall in autumn

appearance.seasonal: deciduous; turns pure clear gold in autumn and drops nearly all at once
appearance.silhouette: tall, gaunt, irregular; open pyramidal crown of a few big upswept limbs when young, broader and craggy with age; a column of gold in autumn
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Ginkgo biloba; Flora of China; Missouri Botanical Garden

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (dioecious, wind-pollinated in spring on short shoots; fertilisation by swimming sperm happens just before or after the seeds fall in early autumn; fleshy seeds 1.5-2 cm with a foul butyric-acid coat, shed with the leaves; kernels eaten cooked, ginkgotoxin in quantity). Counts estimated.
